answer: A new identity joins only after an insurer stakes capital underwriting its uniqueness: if proven a puppet, the stake flows into a compensation lagoon paying the investigators who exposed it. Premiums are priced per identity and each vertex of an underwriter's portfolio is audited separately, so covering N puppets costs N full premiums with no bulk discount. Every exposed fraud echoes through the market, collapsing the careless underwriter's future premiums. An honest agent pays one small premium; a Sybil farmer must buy N policies or corrupt N underwriters, each at real, linear cost.
